terms.gloss: secretly; as a preposition, without the knowledge of
terms.grammar: adverb; preposition with the ablative or accusative
evidence: Caes. BC 2.32: nōn sibi clam vōbīs salūtem fugā petīvit? (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Without someone’s knowledge: clam vōbīs (Traupman), clam patrem.

evidence: Liv. 21.63.9: sine līctōribus profectum clam fūrtim (Lewis & Short)

sources: Lewis & Short: clam
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency (printed page numbers): p. 337.
Quotations marked “Lewis & Short” are given as Lewis & Short cites them, in the house spelling; they have not been checked against a modern edition.
